description: Tauri system-tray daemon app — tray icon + context menu + native notifications, no primary window.

defaults.headline: Starter Foundry Tray Daemon
defaults.subheadline: A background tray-icon app driven by a context menu and native notifications.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick tauri-tray when the app has NO primary window — it lives as a tray icon with a right-click context menu and fires OS notifications. Classic examples: Dropbox sync, 1Password background, a Slack notifier, a build-status watcher. If the user needs a popover panel on click, use tauri-menubar. If they need a real window, use tauri-desktop.
architectureNotes: No webview is shown on startup — the app is effectively headless Rust with a tray surface.
All user interaction is via the tray menu (tauri::menu::Menu) and tauri_plugin_notification for native toast messages.
A hidden utility webview CAN be created lazily if the agent later needs HTML rendering for a settings pane, but the default shape is pure tray.
macOS: activation policy set to Accessory so no dock icon appears.
Windows: startup registers the app in the registry Run key via tauri-plugin-autostart so the tray survives reboots.
components: Tray menu items (Status, Sync now, Open logs, Preferences, Quit).
Optional file-system log writer — tray daemons often need introspection without a UI.
gotchas: macOS: without ActivationPolicy::Accessory you end up with a ghost dock icon AND a tray icon. Always set it in the .setup() handler.
macOS notarization: background daemons still need the hardened runtime + notarization — users see a scary Gatekeeper warning otherwise.

Windows: tray-only apps without a window confuse some antivirus heuristics. Sign the binary with a code-signing cert and submit to Microsoft SmartScreen via Partner Center to avoid SmartScreen warnings.
Notifications on macOS require `NSUserNotificationsUsageDescription` in Info.plist (via tauri.conf.json bundle.macOS) AND the user must grant permission on first send — handle the denial case.
Linux (GNOME 45+): tray icons require the AppIndicator extension. Document this in README — Tauri uses libappindicator under the hood and silently fails on stock GNOME.
If you later add a hidden webview, do NOT ship it as `visible: true` in tauri.conf.json — set `visible: false` and show programmatically, otherwise the window flashes on app start.
integrations: tauri-plugin-autostart — launch at login so the tray survives reboots
tauri-plugin-log — file-based logging since there is no on-screen UI
